column1: # Mutant batch for the shared-clipboard change — Dicta's client for the
# clipstore service: a capture receiver, an on-disk outbox, an HTTP client, a
# flusher, a floating picker and a third button in the bubble's long-press
# reveal.
#   scripts/mutate.sh batch scripts/mutants/shared-clipboard.tsv
# Tab-separated: NAME <TAB> FILE <TAB> FROM <TAB> TO [<TAB> TEST_FILTER]
# FROM must occur EXACTLY ONCE in FILE or the mutant is REFUSED — and a
# REFUSED row reads like a pass, so every FROM below was checked for single
# occurrence before the row was written.
# 🔴 DEFINITIONS ONLY, NEVER RESULTS. A verdict is void the moment the
# tree moves — see scripts/MUTATION-TESTING.md. The verdicts these produced
# live in the pull request for this change, stamped with the commit they were
# measured on.
# 🔴 WHY THIS BATCH EXISTS. NOTHING in this change is regression
# coverage: every file is new, so there is no tree on which any of its tests
# could be watched going red. Every one of them is an invariant guard or a
# characterization test, and a guard nobody has broken on purpose is a guard
# nobody has evidence for. This batch is that evidence.
# 🔴 THE HAZARD CLASS THESE TARGET is the SILENT one: a capture that
# never leaves the phone, a failed read that renders as "your shared clipboard
# is empty", a 401 that deletes the queue one item at a time, a reveal button
# clamped off the bottom of the screen. None of those throws, none logs, and
# each looks exactly like the feature working or the service being down.
# 🔴 m-clip24 IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL, and it is in the batch rather
# than beside it on purpose: a batch in which EVERY mutant SURVIVED is
# indistinguishable from a harness that ran nothing, so one row must be a
# mutation whose kill is already known. Read its verdict first; if it survived,
# every other verdict in the run is void.
# 🔴 Each row changes ONE expression and leaves the branch structure
# intact, so a kill is attributable to that expression and nothing else. In
# particular no row deletes a guard TOGETHER WITH its enclosing condition —
# that proves nothing about the guard and dies for the wrong reason.
# 🔴 TWO VERDICTS FROM THE FIRST RUN OF THIS BATCH DROVE EDITS HERE, and
# both are findings about the HARNESS rather than about the code:
#   * m-clip02 was reported SURVIVED under `dev.zacx.dicta.BubbleClipRevealTest`.
#     It is killed by `BubbleRevealGestureTest`, which MEASURES the container's
#     own growth and compares it against the sum of the three dp-derived blocks
#     — the only test that computes the two sides independently. The clip
#     picker's own clamp tests build their expected sum FROM clipBlockPx, so an
#     UNDERSTATED block is invisible to them by construction. A `-run` filter
#     that excludes the killing test reports SURVIVED; the filter is widened to
#     `dev.zacx.dicta.Bubble*Test`, not the test weakened.
#   * m-clip17's original mutation — rank-the-whole-list instead of
#     filter-row-by-row — is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT, which is why it survived.
#     `SnipMatcher.rank` partitions into declared-term hits and label hits and
#     returns `declared + labeled`; `ClipPickerActivity.searchViewOf` builds its
#     synthetic Snippet with `searchTerms = emptyList()`, so `declared` is
#     ALWAYS empty and rank degrades to a stable filter. There is no ordering
#     to leak. Replaced with a mutation that genuinely reorders
#     (`rows.sortedBy { it.body }`), which the server-order test kills.
# 🔴 TEST_FILTER is an optimisation and the harness refuses a run that
# executed zero tests, which is what makes a typo'd filter fail loudly instead
# of reading as SURVIVED. Without that guard the column would be unsafe.
